facts: The middle ceiling, for countries that are heavy anonymizing-egress geographies AND have a large population of ordinary users.

The abuse in SG was real, but it was a *domain* farm rather than a country: ~160 accounts on dhisy/dewaa/sendang/yotube/gusil, now priced by `flaggedEmailDomain` instead. Catching it there is what makes this tier affordable.
The reasons that show `FREEBUFF_RESTRICTED_NOTICE`. `third_party_client` stays on the cause-blind `FREEBUFF_CAPACITY_NOTICE` on purpose: it is a detector worth not naming.

Deliberately says nothing about the account. It names the thing that ran out (today's free usage), not a property of the person, and it does not use "limited", "restricted" or "blocked", those read as a verdict, and they are the words that generate "is my account restricted?" tickets.
Rates below are "share of the domain's accounts carrying an automated ban, honeypot hit, or foreign-toolset detection". Baselines from the same window: gmail.com 5%, proton.me 7%, outlook.com 23%.
entries.title: Shared/Core update: freebuff-spend-ceilings

ai.title: Singapore Singapore spend ceiling split from restricted CN cap
ai.summary: Split Singapore out of the restricted-country list: FREEBUFF_RESTRICTED_COUNTRIES now contains only CN, while a new FREEBUFF_ELEVATED_COUNTRIES=['SG'] pair pairs a new FREEBUFF_ELEVATED_DAILY_SPEND_USD=5 ceiling with the elevated_country reason in resolveFreebuffSpendCeiling. The split lets SG ordinary users keep a working day instead of a 30x lower cap, with the SG domain farm (dhisy.com, dewaa.id, sendang.space, yotube.id, gusil.my.id) instead caught by flaggedEmailDomain. A new FREEBUFF_BUDGET_NOTICE and FREEBUFF_BUDGET_NOTICE_REASONS give region, elevated_country, and trust_level refusals a plain allowance message that says nothing about the account's behavior.
ai.evidence: In common/src/constants/freebuff-spend-ceilings.ts, FREEBUFF_RESTRICTED_COUNTRIES changed from ['SG', 'CN'] to ['CN'], and the new exports FREEBUFF_ELEVATED_DAILY_SPEND_USD = 5, FREEBUFF_ELEVATED_COUNTRIES = ['SG'], FREEBUFF_BUDGET_NOTICE_REASONS, and FREEBUFF_BUDGET_NOTICE were added; freebuffSpendNoticeFor now return FREEBUFF_BUDGET_NOTICE for region/elevated_country/trust_level reasons, and resolveFreebuffSpendCeiling applies an elevated_country rule. In common/src/util/disposable-email.ts, DISPOSABLE_EMAIL_DOMAINS grew by dhisy.com, dewaa.id, sendang.space, yotube.id, and gusil.my.id, and domainOf formatting changed.

facts: ("Policy Violation: this user has been blocked") and took Luna to a 100% failure rate with four usable endpoints sitting under the ceiling.
OpenRouter provider slug Luna prefers (first in `provider.order`).

- It must stay under the next tier up. Azure, Azure EU and Amazon Bedrock listed $1.00/$6.00 when this was written and re-priced to $0.20/$1.20 by 2026-08-16; the ceiling admits them at today's price and would exclude them again if they returned to the old one.

The headroom covers OpenAI's own tiers (list $0.10/$0.60, priority $0.20/$1.20, flex $0.05/$0.30) and ordinary price drift, while still failing closed well before a 10x endpoint could serve a request.

Error branch first, see the chat model's schema for why: an error chunk that also carries `choices` otherwise matches the normal branch and has its `error` key stripped, silently turning a stated provider failure into an empty stream.
entries.title: Shared/Core update: freebuff-models
entries.summary: Shared/Core, LLM Providers changes across 3 file(s) (+126/−44).

ai.title: Luna routing switches to preferred provider order with price ceiling
ai.summary: GPT-5.6 Luna's routing in common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts is no longer a hard provider pin; the FREEBUFF_GPT_5_6_LUNA_PROVIDER_ROUTE doc now describes OpenAI as the preferred slug (first in `provider.order`), and the routing decision is bounded by FREEBUFF_GPT_5_6_LUNA_MAX_PRICE ({prompt:0.5, completion:3.0}) as a cost fence rather than allow_fallbacks:false, because OpenAI began refusing every Luna request with 'Policy Violation: this user has been blocked' on 2026-08-16, leaving a 100% failure rate with four usable endpoints under the ceiling. The chat model's createOpenAICompatibleChatChunkSchema and the completion model's createOpenAICompatibleCompletionChunkSchema both move the errorSchema branch to first in the z.union so an error chunk that also carries an empty `choices` array is not masked by the normal-chunk branch (which z.object strips of the `error` key), preventing a stated provider refusal from collapsing into an empty stream.
ai.evidence: common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts edits the JSDoc on FREEBUFF_GPT_5_6_LUNA_MODEL_ID and FREEBUFF_GPT_5_6_LUNA_PROVIDER_ROUTE (comment now reads 'OpenRouter provider slug Luna prefers (first in `provider.order`)') and rewrites the FREEBUFF_GPT_5_6_LUNA_MAX_PRICE doc from a hard provider pin to a cost fence that must stay above list and under the next tier; openai-compatible-chat-language-model.ts reorders createOpenAICompatibleChatChunkSchema so errorSchema is the first union member; openai-compatible-completion-language-model.ts does the same for createOpenAICompatibleCompletionChunkSchema; test 'surfaces a provider error chunk that also carries empty choices' asserts the streamed error is surfaced and finishReason is 'error'.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the openrouter.ts code that enforces `provider.order` or `provider.max_price`, nor which consumer reads the reworded constant docs at runtime.

changes.what: Reworked the FREEBUFF_GPT_5_6_LUNA_MODEL_ID, FREEBUFF_GPT_5_6_LUNA_PROVIDER_ROUTE, and FREEBUFF_GPT_5_6_LUNA_MAX_PRICE documentation from a hard provider pin to a preferred-provider-order plus price-ceiling cost fence, after OpenAI began blocking all Luna requests.

Reordered the streaming chunk Zod schema unions in both the chat and completion OpenAI-compatible models so the error branch resolves first, so a provider refusal that ships alongside an empty choices array is surfaced as an error instead of being stripped into an empty stream.

facts: The root Freebuff Desktop's AUTO-RUN decider runs under: the agent that picks what a tab on Auto does next when a turn ends with nothing queued (see freebuff-desktop/src/server/services/autorun.ts). It is not the working agent, it never edits files or runs commands, it only chooses the next input.
("Out of credits") for the entire free-mode population, which is most of Desktop, auto-run simply never produced a next step for them.
The Desktop auto-run decider. Spawns nothing, but the hierarchy gate reads this list for the ROOT itself, and a decision has no parent run to hang off.

The auto-run decider reads the same set for the same reason: it decides on the tab's own model, which is the one that tab's session was admitted with. Pinning it to a single model instead would 403 every tab on any other one.
entries.title: Shared/Core update: free-agents

ai.title: Freebuff Desktop auto-run decider registered as free-mode root agent
ai.summary: A new constant `FREEBUFF_DESKTOP_AUTORUN_AGENT_ID = 'freebuff-desktop-autorun'` is defined and added to `FREEBUFF_ROOT_AGENT_IDS` in common/src/constants/free-agents.ts so the Desktop auto-run decider (freebuff-desktop/src/server/services/autorun.ts) is admitted as a first-party free-mode root. It is mapped to `FREEBUFF_DESKTOP_MODELS` in `FREE_MODE_AGENT_MODELS` so it can run on the tab's own model rather than being pinned to one, which previously 403'd with `session_model_mismatch`. The opening line 'You are Buffy, the auto-run agent behind Freebuff Desktop.' is appended to `FREEBUFF_ROOT_SYSTEM_PROMPT_OPENINGS` so the decider's prompt - which states it never edits files or runs commands - is distinguished from base3's coding-agent opening.
ai.evidence: common/src/constants/free-agents.ts adds the exported constant `FREEBUFF_DESKTOP_AUTORUN_AGENT_ID = 'freebuff-desktop-autorun'`, appends it to `FREEBUFF_ROOT_AGENT_IDS`, and maps it to `FREEBUFF_DESKTOP_MODELS` in `FREE_MODE_AGENT_MODELS`; it also appends a new entry to `FREEBUFF_ROOT_SYSTEM_PROMPT_OPENINGS`: 'You are Buffy, the auto-run agent behind Freebuff Desktop.'
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the consumer change in autorun.ts that reads this list or how the decider's model is now resolved at runtime.

ai.title: Remove NEXTPUBLICHUMANBEHAVIORINGESTIONURL
ai.summary: Removed NEXT_PUBLIC_HUMANBEHAVIOR_INGESTION_URL from clientEnvSchema and clientProcessEnv in common/src/env-schema.ts. The SDK's default ingestion host is now enforced, eliminating the option to point deployments at non-default Human Behavior endpoints. This change affects shared core environment validation. Developers must ensure their deployments use the standard ingestion URL.

eli5.text: The system no longer lets operators redirect certain analytics traffic to custom server addresses they chose themselves; traffic of this kind now always goes to the standard destination the system picks by default. This affects teams that run the software who had previously pointed this traffic at their own alternate endpoints. If you looked right now, you would see that the option to set those alternate addresses has disappeared from the configuration, so any such redirection you set up will be ignored.
